content.text:
IPv6 host brackets are now kept literal in link destinations: `[visit](http://[2001:db8::1]/)` renders as `<a href="http://[2001:db8::1]/">`. The markdown-it suite (305 tests, including 5 new ones) and the CommonMark spec suite pass; the type-check and lint commands were denied permission here, so those two did not run.

**Cause:** `normalizeLink` in `src/markdownit.ts` percent-encoded the whole formatted URL, and `[` / `]` are not in the encoder's safe-character list, so the host brackets were encoded along with everything else.

**Fix:** when the parsed hostname looks like an IPv6 literal (only hex digits, dots and at least one colon), `normalizeLink` now encodes the parts before and after the host separately and puts the host back in literal brackets. Brackets in the path, query or fragment are still encoded as before, e.g. `/a[b]` → `/a%5Bb%5D`.

A bracketed host that is not IPv6-shaped, such as `http://[foo]/`, behaves as it did before (rendered as `http://foo/`).

The new test cases are appended to `test/fixtures/markdown-it/normalize.txt` and cover inline links, autolinks, reference definitions, a URL with auth and port, and the non-IPv6 case.
